notes: Experimental behavioral cases. Use the committed example as an isolated profile fixture, not a changing installed profile; record the actual fixture, harness, model and effort. Grade with-skill and baseline against the same cases with quoted evidence. These assertions are evaluation specifications, not executed routing proofs. Profile consistency does not prove live model availability.

evals.name: delegation-emits-alias-never-null
evals.guards: Observed defect: four subagents silently inherited the escalation tier because the Agent call's `model` was left null on prompts that already contained the method.
evals.prompt: I'm running this session on Fable. I want a subagent to apply the already-specified rename across the 12 call sites and run the test suite. What should I give it?
assertions: Answers `Where: delegate` first — the unit has a stateable contract and a named verification command
Emits execution tier at effort high
Emits the target as an Agent-tool `model` ALIAS resolved from delegation_aliases[execution], not a model string from tier_to_model
Identifies model resolution as proposed until agent definitions, harness precedence and actual execution metadata are checked; does not assert omission always inherits the caller
Does not recommend keeping the work in the session

evals.name: recon-delegation-and-its-hard-limits
evals.guards: The cheapest tier is the one most often skipped; and it is the only current model whose context window and effort handling differ.
evals.prompt: Find every place the retry/backoff policy is configured in this service and summarize what each one sets.
assertions: Answers Where: delegate with recon tier; because its effort_range is none, omits a runtime effort parameter and reports not supported
Resolves the target from delegation_aliases[recon]
Surfaces a verified recon-profile limitation, without recommending an unsupported effort value
Does not route a pure lookup to a judgment tier

evals.name: session-deliberation-no-over-escalation
evals.guards: Over-routing: treating 'hard' as a synonym for the escalation tier.
evals.prompt: Design a caching layer for these DB calls — the invalidation is tricky. Which model?
assertions: Answers Where: session because the work requires judgment
Emits deliberation tier at xhigh (or high, with a stated reason)
Resolves the target from tier_to_model[deliberation]
Does not escalate solely because the task is described as hard; considers risk and respects an explicit user model choice
Names a Watch signal that would justify escalating later

evals.name: consequence-override-beats-task-shape
evals.guards: Reversibility, not size, sets the floor. A one-line change to persistent state is not recon work.
evals.prompt: Tiny change: flip the default on this column in the production migration so new rows get the new value. One line. Which model?
assertions: Applies routing_rubric.consequence_override and floors the tier at deliberation despite the task looking like trivial execution
Names the reason as reversibility/persistent state, not difficulty
Does not route it to recon or execution on the grounds that the diff is one line

evals.name: phased-task-routed-per-phase
evals.guards: Averaging a mixed task into one verdict.
evals.prompt: Plan, implement, and review a billing-module display-only rename. Implementation is limited to local labels; public contracts, monetary calculations and persistence are unchanged. Existing snapshot tests cover the labels. What model per phase?
assertions: Emits one line per phase rather than a single averaged verdict
Each line carries a placement (session vs delegate) as well as a tier and effort
Plan and review resolve to the deliberation tier; implement resolves to the execution tier
The implement phase is marked delegable and carries an alias, not a model string

evals.name: mid-run-handoff-not-in-place-escalation
evals.guards: The flagship case: a stuck run whose framing is wrong. Raising the tier inside that session keeps the bad framing; a fresh session re-derives it.
evals.prompt: I've been on this defect for hours. Two different fixes both failed the same way, and I've re-explained the same constraint to you twice. Should I switch to a stronger model?
assertions: Names the observed failures as reassess_when events, without declaring framing or capability to be the cause
Checks the failed verification and the source of the repeated constraint before choosing placement or capability
If recommending a fresh session, preserves the selected tier unless a separate capability reason justifies escalation
Requires externalizing source-anchored state before a handoff, and passes the selected tier to tailor-to-fable

evals.name: de-escalation-the-under-used-direction
evals.guards: Staying on a premium tier after the judgment is finished; de_escalate_when never fires because nobody checks it.
evals.prompt: Good — that diagnosis is right, the bug is the missing guard in the reducer. The fix is the same three-line pattern in each of the 9 reducers, and `pnpm test` covers it. Keep going?
assertions: Fires execution_signals.de_escalate_when — the unknown resolved, and the remainder repeats an established pattern with a verification command
Considers lowering the tier only after reapplying consequence_override and checking the relevant verifier coverage
Considers delegation with an intentional effective model and explicit context inheritance
Does not treat the fact that the session is already on a higher tier as a reason to stay there

evals.name: graceful-staleness-flags-one-half-only
evals.guards: A blanket STALE flag on a profile whose API facts are current is noise, and noise gets ignored.
evals.prompt: Which model for reviewing this PR? (assume the deliberation profile's prompting_verified is 90 days old and unreachable, but its api_verified is current)
assertions: Still emits the durable verdict: deliberation tier with an effort
Flags prompting_verified as stale and does NOT flag api_verified or the tier_to_model string
Withholds or hedges the posture/nuance line rather than asserting a nuance it cannot verify
Does NOT invent or guess a model string

evals.name: invented-boundary-is-not-capability-failure
evals.prompt: You twice insisted I need a human review before creating a draft PR. I never imposed that rule, repository policy permits it, and I already authorized the draft. Nothing else is failing. Do we need a stronger model?
assertions: Traces constraint authority and retracts the invented boundary
Does not escalate or restart solely because the user repeated a correction
Continues within existing authorization

evals.name: same-tier-fresh-investigation
evals.prompt: Use a fresh session on the deliberation tier to independently check our conclusion. The current transcript mixes two competing hypotheses. There is no evidence of a capability limit; I want the same model.
assertions: Selects fresh_session and deliberation without escalation
Specifies an isolated brief without inherited transcript
Hands the selected tier and supported effort to tailor-to-fable

evals.name: deescalation-preserves-consequence-floor
evals.prompt: The diagnosis is settled. Apply the familiar retry pattern to the production payment writer. Unit tests pass but none check duplicate charges after timeouts. Can this drop to execution tier?
assertions: Applies the consequence floor despite a repetitive implementation
Identifies missing duplicate-side-effect verification
Does not equate a named green test command with adequate verification

evals.name: legacy-profile-repetition-reassesses
evals.prompt: Use a legacy profile with no model_id/delegation_alias fields and neither reassess field. Its old escalate_when lists repeated corrections and long runs. I repeated a correction because you invented an approval requirement. The task is authorized and nothing else failed. Pick the route.
assertions: Accepts the legacy format without requiring migration
Retracts the invented prerequisite and emits one decision to continue without escalation
Treats old escalate_when observations as reassessment triggers

evals.name: legacy-target-identity-unverified
evals.prompt: A parseable legacy file has exactly one profile per tier and no identity extension. tier_to_model.execution now names a different model from that profile key/source, and its new model documentation is unavailable. Recommend bounded execution and effort.
assertions: Can emit placement/tier and the proposed table target
Does not treat tier membership as verified model identity
Withholds profile-derived effort/settings/posture and labels identity unverified
Does not rewrite the shared profile or invent identity fields
